That’s the signal of confidence I like to see: $COHR issues a new $2B share buyback, through open market purchases.

Optical industry looks very undervalued right now, especially as it reaches the inflection of the next supercycle.

We’re already seeing photonics-SOI substrate players go from $25M revenue -> $1.2B LTAs signed in a quarter.

Or $100M backlog -> $500M in a quarter with InP substrates.

And we’ll see acceleration for lasers, modules, and the optical supply chain next.

I’m sure Coherent finds its own valuation very low now too, especially after signing $20B LTAs recently.

Markets have now given me PTSD on every green rally.

That being said, $SOI accelerating from $25m quarterly photonics-SOI revenue… with no forward visibility earlier this year.

Into securing $1.2B in agreements this quarter, backed by cash, is extremely transformative and make me happy to see.

In terms transcript details:

- “AI data center have built large compute power, but some of it remains idle as copper links limit data availability for processing. 

Optics removes that bottleneck”

Reiterating what I said about aggregate capex not applying 1:1 with optical sector, given optical shifts improves GPU utilization

- timelines: “Near-package optics brings first volume by the end of the fiscal year, and high volume next year. 

Co-Packaged Optics for scale out is starting to ramp. TPO for scale up will be the next stage”

- “Growth comes in waves, scale out and scale up as a new driver. As those links goes optical, they create new volume on top of today's. 

In fiscal year 2027, our revenue comes mostly from pluggable transceiver, and we see initial volume from NPO.”

- “Growth returned sooner than we had anticipated and with more vigor. Revenue grew 39%, with Photonics-SOI leading the way.

Margin expansion has come forward too”

- “So, for the capacity reservation agreement we signed, they cover calendar year 2027, calendar year 2028, and beyond”

In terms of where they see acceleration:

- “Now we see and we believe the new requests that we are getting lately are more for the Co-Packaged Optics and NPO. And especially for the scale-up going forward.”

I think that this quarter earnings marks the inflection of optical acceleration for Soitec + silicon photonics.

And what it means for a chokepoint to transform into company economics.

Gartner has cyber spending growth slowing to 11.2% next year.

I think that's way too low.

The outages put cyber back on everyone’s radar. The reason I think spending follows is that hackers are getting faster than the patch cycles companies still rely on. Anthropic is cutting its disclosure window for serious bugs from 90 days to 30 because another model can find the same flaw while the first vendor is still working on a fix.

So what does the extra budget buy? Finding exposed systems earlier, testing fixes faster, and containing the flaws you can’t patch without taking something critical offline. Anne Neuberger wants AI labs helping critical infrastructure operators do exactly that. I think those labs could end up capturing a meaningful slice of the cyber budget. And honestly there is a good chance that one of the biggest cyber companies of the next decade might be an AI lab.

$OSPN is one way we approached this at @AsymmetricBets_  Bets. Even if a hacker gets past the login, the bank still has to verify who approved the wire.

With semis and AI infra under pressure, I still think $BUG has legs into year-end.

Everyone frames custom chips as Google and Meta escaping Nvidia's toll booth. Look at who they're escaping to.

Hock Tan bought VMware for ~$69B, killed the perpetual licenses and pushed everyone onto bundles. AT&T told a court its renewal quote went up 1,050%. Customers screamed for a year, and most of them paid anyway, because ripping VMware out of a data center is worse than eating the bill.

That's the same guy co-designing Google's TPUs, Meta's chips and OpenAI's 10GW custom silicon deal. With VMware he found something customers couldn't easily rip out and priced it that way, and he's been doing some version of that his whole career.

Once your model stack is tuned to a chip only one shop can build for you, leaving gets about as painful as leaving VMware was, and he's the one who'll be quoting you the renewal for the next decade.
